title: getSessionId fragmentation: 7 implementations with 4 distinct fallback semantics in hooks src; shared barrel re-exports the ppid-scheme under the canonical name

evidence.quote:
getResourceFilePath,
  getSessionId,
  DEFAULT_RESOURCE_STATE,
import { getSessionId, getProject } from './shared/session-id.js';
import { getSessionStatePath, getStatePathWithMigration, cleanupOldStateFiles } from './shared/session-isolation.js';

observe_how: Caller map (non-test src). Scheme A session-id.ts (COORDINATION_SESSION_ID env > ~/.claude/.coordination-session-id file > BRAINTRUST_SPAN_ID > s-<ts36>): file-claims.ts, heartbeat.ts, session-register.ts, session-start-parallel.ts; composed into getBusId by session-bus-id.ts which feeds context-bus.ts default bus id. Scheme B session-isolation.ts (CLAUDE_SESSION_ID > hostname-PID): maestro-cleanup, maestro-enforcer, maestro-state-manager, plan-exit-tracker, plan-to-ralph-enforcer, ralph-delegation-enforcer, smarter-everyday (7 hooks via state-path helpers). Scheme C private clones (CLAUDE_SESSION_ID > ppid/pid/undefined variants): guardrail-enforcer.ts:98, lib/hook-trace.ts:34, shared/logger.ts:72, shared/resource-reader.ts:70. NEW beyond SEED-12's '2 competing schemes': the 4 private clones, and shared/index.ts:101 re-exports resource-reader's ppid-scheme as the barrel's `getSessionId` — any future `import { getSessionId } from './shared/index.js'` silently gets a per-process ppid id, not the coordination id. Consequence: state files, traces, guardrail acks, and coordination rows for the SAME session carry non-joinable ids.
telemetry: corr-null 60.7% on intel-bus rows is consistent with id-scheme mismatch across emitting hooks; hook-trace.jsonl sessionId (pid-based) can never join sessions table ids (s-<ts36>).
